question: Can one 5.12 client run a 3D session without any mission phases (the Sharp3D route) and why does it still reach every login step?

status: answered (lab 4.20r6 single client + third-party capture): our gserver runs the MISSION-PHASES entry route, not the phase-free route. Login order: "Graal has been activated!" -> "Loading tile definitions for server Login" -> "Phase 1: Download Ghost Objects" (GhostAlways rides INSIDE Phase 1: GhostAlwaysStarting->ghosts->GhostAlwaysDone after DataBlocksDone) -> "Phase 2: Mission Lighting"->done -> "Initial Control Object" (control arrives, the 3D GUI GuiGraal3DCtrl attaches as the scene renders). The phase-free (ghost-always-only) route is real -- captured on a third-party server (live-512-third-party-session) -- but our gserver always sends MissionStartPhase1/2/3 with GhostAlways nested in Phase 1; a phase-free variant needs a gserver emit mode we do not enable. The client reaches the same login steps either way because GhostAlways delivery is common to both, only the phase framing differs. torque/3d-session-entry-route-420r6-2026-11-26.md, torque/live-512-third-party-session-2026-11-24.md

question: Does the server time field drive any visible client behaviour (animations, timevar3, day/night)?

status: answered (lab 4.20r6 single client): the server time field drives timevar3, a synchronized Graal3D clock (server+client, ms) that advances continuously ~1/sec and ANIMATES SMOOTHLY (not a jump), feeding the day/night drawing mode. A weapon read per second: timevar = coarse integer tick (2->7->15); timevar2 = UNIX wall-clock (~1.7956e9); timevar3 = synced Graal3D time (~12->40->80 across the run). A changed server time re-syncs timevar3 (stays server-driven) rather than letting it free-run. For a server: drive day/night/timed 3D effects via timevar3 read continuously from the server time field. torque/3d-server-time-timevar3-420r6-2026-11-26.md

status: answered (static bin + lab): the fxSunLight animation-switch group is 14 flags, NOT 16 -- settled. The 5.12 Graal3DEngine registers exactly 14 boolean animation-switch fields in order (anim colour/brightness/rotation/size/azimuth/elevation, lerp colour/brightness/rotation/size/azimuth/elevation, link flare size, single colour keys); nothing resembling a 15th/16th flag follows -- the next fields are the 8 key strings and 6 cycle times (pstring/float, not flags), and enable/flaretp are separate raw-8 fields. question: How close is our renderer to each real client in the same scene: camera fov and near/far, fog curve, lighting, texture filtering, mip levels, alpha sorting?

status: answered (lab 4.20r6, fidelity): g3d-replay is a schematic POSITIONAL debug view (a box per GameObject + a 2-unit ground grid + a flat two-colour sky tinted with the Sky fog colour, near=0.1), NOT a pixel-faithful renderer -- it matches the real client on NONE of the five features. Real 4.20r6: textured+filtered+mipmapped .3ds, per-face directional Sun lighting + specular, real mesh geometry, sky gradient, distance fog (EXT_fog_coord), depth-sorted alpha. g3d-replay: no meshes/textures/lighting/distance-fog/alpha. Per feature all DIFFER: camera FOV/near-far (positions approximate only), fog curve (none; only a flat sky tint), lighting (flat unlit boxes), texture filtering/mips (no textures), alpha sorting (opaque boxes). The stand-in is intentional until the real Torque renderer lands (T3D-122). For a server: use the real 4.20r6 client for look/feel; g3d-replay is a positional/topology sanity view only. Method: real client live-rendered; g3d-replay derived from its source (view3d.cpp) as no Linux binary exists and the Windows build is out of scope. torque/3d-fidelity-g3dreplay-vs-client-420r6-2026-11-26.md

question: How does the client recover from partial or bad data mid-session: a truncated download, a ghost update for an unknown object, a dropped TerrainChunkEvent, a server restart?
why_it_matters: Servers will send bad data sometimes.
how_to_test: Lab: cut each stream at a point on our gserver; note crash, skip or resync.
status: answered (lab Linux 4.20r6): fail-soft, not self-healing. Truncated download: cached 'done' at wrong size, asset left blank, no re-request/hang/crash, link kept; a later complete send is never fetched. Unknown 2D instance update: silently ignored (vs unknown class, which drops the link). Server restart: instant drop to login, no auto-reconnect even though the server is listening again; no crash. Dropped terrain chunk: not drivable (server emits no terrain). See torque/3d-recovery-420r6-2026-11-25.md

question: What is the common subset of 3D content that 4.04r2, 4.20r8 and 5.12 all draw, so one world can serve all three?

status: answered (lab, 4.20r6 proto 24 + 4.04r2 proto 19 run; 5.00r7 relied on prior note): common drawable content is Sky + Sun lighting + a shape + a Camera. No single byte stream: the gserver splits at the protocol 19/24 boundary from one world file - protocol 19 = TGE datablocks + stock Player/Camera + 3-phase start (no Sun ghost); protocol 24 = GameObject + Sun ghost + 2-phase start. One authored world, two server-side encodings. A lone protocol-19 client only sees its own first-person avatar; to show world shapes to 4.04r2 the server would need to ghost them as Players/StaticShapes (not done today). See torque/3d-shared-world-subset-2026-11-25.md

question: Which 3D state lives on the server and which only on the client (positions, physics, collision, animation, sky, lighting), and what does the client trust from itself?

Client-trusts-self (reported ~2.5 UDP updates/s, not corrected by default) = its own control-object position/state and its camera prediction; a g3dpos override snaps it and the client ignores its own reports ~2 s. Shared = the control object. Not testable on this route (no terrain/no movement): local physics/collision; animation (no sequence sent). See torque/3d-state-authority-420r6-2026-11-25.md

question: What is the largest texture dimension the 5.12-class client loads and draws, and what does it do past that limit (reject, white, downscale, crash)?
why_it_matters: Servers need the safe texture-size ceiling for 3D assets.
how_to_test: Lab 4.20r6 single client: ramp a GameObject's texture 256->8192 px (power-of-two and non-PoT); screenshot each.
status: answered (lab 4.20r6 single client, software GL): a GameObject texture draws at full fidelity from 256 up to and including 8192x8192; by 10240px the client crashes silently on texture load — no downscale, no white fallback, no error line, not an OS OOM-kill; non-power-of-two textures are accepted and drawn like PoT; the ceiling is client-imposed (the 32-bit process address space during in-process decode + llvmpipe system-memory copy), NOT the GL driver limit (llvmpipe reports GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE 16384, above where the client dies at 10240/12288); the ~8192 safe figure is a software-GL + 32-bit-client ceiling, 16384 the hard GL ceiling a 64-bit/real-GPU path would approach; server takeaway: keep shape textures <=8192; torque/3d-texture-size-limit-420r6-2026-11-26.md

question: How does the 5.12-class file loader handle a malformed on-disk asset (truncated, zero-byte, oversized, wrong magic) for a texture, a font and a sound fetched over the Graal file protocol?
why_it_matters: Error handling for bad server assets on a single client.
how_to_test: Lab 4.20r6 single client: place deliberately broken .png/.ttf/.wav; observe white/skip/not-found/crash and console.
status: answered (lab 4.20r6 single client): on-disk file-loader error paths. Only the FONT loader crashes — a malformed .ttf (truncated, zero-byte, or wrong-magic text) takes the client down at startup, before it connects (font loaded eagerly at start-up, no empty/short guard; even zero-byte crashes). The texture loader is robust: bad magic/empty -> untextured white cube, truncated/CRC-broken -> partially-decoded garbled cube drawn anyway, scene always survives. The sound loader is robust: broken .wav (truncated/empty/non-RIFF) -> silent no-op, FMOD inits and play runs, scene survives. With T3D-118 the two file-level crash paths are an oversized texture (>~8192px) and a broken font; malformed small textures and sounds are low-risk; torque/3d-file-loader-errors-420r6-2026-11-26.md

question: Which font files and formats does showtext/GUI text fetch and accept on the 5.12-class client, how is the name resolved, and what is the fallback when the font is missing?
why_it_matters: HUD/overlay text needs known font packaging rules.
how_to_test: Lab 4.20r6 single client: showtext with present/missing/alt-format fonts; list fetched files; screenshot.
status: answered (lab 4.20r6 single client): showtext resolves a font to lowercase(family) + a weight/slant suffix (bd bold, i italic with it fallback, bi bold-italic, none plain) + .ttf, requested over the Graal file protocol; alignment letters do not change the filename; passing an extension yields name.ttf.ttf. Only TrueType is accepted (the client ships arial.ttf; resolution always appends .ttf; no bitmap font path). A validly-absent font falls back to the default (shipped Arial) and the text still draws — no crash (graceful counterpart to the T3D-119 malformed-font startup crash). A font must be pre-placed on disk to apply: an on-demand first fetch caches it to levels/fonts/<name>.ttf (with extension, unlike textures under levels3d/images without extension, T3D-090) but the triggering draw still falls back to default — the too-late-this-session pattern; torque/3d-font-handling-420r6-2026-11-26.md

question: Does the unpacked Windows 6.00 engine carry the same protocol-24 3D networked class set as 5.12 (GameObject + the ~28 classes), or did the 3D class set / protocol change again at v6?
why_it_matters: Whether a v6 client is a 5.12-class 3D client or a new lineage decides server support for v6.
how_to_test: Static: compare the 6.00r2/6.00r4 unpacked engine's registered 3D/networked class set and protocol markers against 5.12 (T3D-081), conceptual only.
status: answered (static, bin): the unpacked Windows 6.00 engine is NOT a 5.12-class protocol-24 3D client — it is the native "Quattro" 2D Graal engine (classic gen-5 2D protocol, low-PLI id set, TServer*/TGaniObject/TGraalVar object model, TSocket session) that never carried the Torque GameObject + proto-24 3D class set; GameObject, TerrainBlock, WaterBlock, Torque Sky/Sun/Camera and the whole Torque networked layer (GameConnection/NetConnection/SimObject/datablocks/.mis/.ter/.dts/.dif/.dso) are absent, as are the 11 TGE content classes (never carried, vs dropped on 5.12); the shared Graal GS2 shell and the GuiGraal3DCtrl NAME survive (a 2D playfield control, no scene graph) but TParticleEmitter/play2/play3d are absent; levels3d/graal3:// are inert vestiges; so a 6.00 client speaks the classic 2D protocol and has no 3D classes to ghost; torque/3d-v6-quattro-vs-512-2026-11-26.md ALSO confirmed on the ORIGINAL 6.03r7 (v6.037) Windows client, read directly (unpacked, token G3D0311C): zero Torque-3D classes (no GameObject/TerrainBlock/WaterBlock/SimObject/NetConnection/ShapeBase/TSShape/Sky/Sun/Camera), full 2D Quattro object model present, GS2 shell intact, engine names itself Quattro; no separate Graal3DEngine.dll (3D would be in the one exe, and is not); vs 6.00 the GuiGraal3DCtrl vestige NAME is gone (only graal3://, levels3d survive) and a 2D particle system (TParticleEmitter/TParticleVarModifier) + Flash/RTMP media layer are present, all 2D; same note.

question: How does our Frankenstein 6.037 build differ from the stock 6.00 Quattro engine, and does it carry any Torque/3D capability stock 6.00 lacks?
why_it_matters: Our own 6.037 build is what we'd ship/test; need to know if it is 3D-capable at all.
how_to_test: Static: compare our 6.037 build's engine/class/protocol surface against stock 6.00 (T3D-121) and 5.12; note any grafted Torque 3D classes, protocol-24 markers, or GS2 3D additions.
status: answered (static, bin): our "Frankenstein 6.037" is NOT stock 6.00 and not a patched binary but our own from-source hybrid — a 6.03r7 Quattro 2D host (the stock-6.00 lineage, T3D-121) with our 5.12 Graal3D protocol-24 link linked directly in; names itself Frankenstein 6.0/6.037, version 0.0.1, unpacked with ordinary C++ symbols, no Themida/QPlay packer. Unlike stock 6.00 (2D-only) it ADDS a whole proto-24 3D stack: enters a "3 " server on two links at once (UDP on port+1, TCP login on the listed port, as 5.12), runs the handshake + login steps 2-6, ghosts GameObject and Camera + the initial control object + movement + sky state + terrain chunks, and bridges 3D-link server text to the 6.x GS2 machine (UDP left enabled, unlike stock 6.x). NOT yet added: the real Torque world renderer (terrain/interiors/DTS/.3ds/sky textures) — it reads the 3D world but draws only a stand-in box/grid placeholder; also no 3D movement keys / 6.x server list / gserver 3D lab run yet. Verdict: it CAN be driven as a 5.12-class proto-24 3D client (box-view only), emphatically not stock-6.00 repacked; torque/3d-frankenstein-6037-vs-600-2026-11-26.md

question: Which sound formats does the 5.12-class client actually resolve and play via play/play2 (wav, ogg, mp3, mod/other), and what happens with an unsupported format?
why_it_matters: Server sound packaging needs the accepted format list, lab-confirmed.
how_to_test: Lab 4.20r6 single client: one file per format via play2; record fetch/resolve + FMOD accept/reject (audio not verifiable headless).
status: answered (lab 4.20r6 + bin): the audio backend is FMOD 3.70 (libfmod-3.70.so, FMOD 3.x not FMOD Ex 4.x), whose native decodable set is exactly WAV/MP2/MP3/OGG/WMA/ASF (the T3D-062 static list), no FLAC/AAC. Lab via play2: WAV/OGG/MP3/MP2 resolve (PLI_UPDATEFILE) and are accepted with no error (the reliable cross-platform set); WMA/ASF are named in the build but are the Windows-only Media codec, undependable on this Linux client (resolve, no error, but almost certainly do not decode — the one uncertain row); FLAC/AAC resolve but FMOD 3.70 cannot decode them. Every format supported or not is handled gracefully: resolve + a silent no-op for the undecodable, no error, no crash (matches T3D-119). Audio not verifiable headless (no per-sound FMOD result is logged, even for known-good WAV) so the accept/reject split rests on the FMOD 3.70 codec set + strings, not heard audio. For a server: ship WAV/OGG/MP3/MP2; avoid WMA/ASF and FLAC/AAC; torque/3d-sound-formats-420r6-2026-11-26.md

question: What is the largest .3ds mesh (vertex/face count) the 5.12-class client draws before failure, and the failure mode, beyond the known u16 vertex cap?
why_it_matters: Shape budget ceiling for 3D assets, companion to the texture ceiling (T3D-118).
how_to_test: Lab 4.20r6 single client: ramp a single GameObject mesh's vertex/face count to and past the u16 cap; screenshot and console.
status: answered (lab 4.20r6 single client, software GL, 32-bit client): two draw limits, never a crash. (1) .3ds FORMAT cap: 16-bit vertex/face counts per chunk, so the face count caps first at ~65535 faces (~33k verts) — a chunk draws to the cap (65522 faces drew), past it the field wraps and the shape silently draws nothing. (2) per-SHAPE total-geometry draw ceiling: a multi-chunk shape can exceed 65535 verts (66k drew) but draws only to ~265k verts/~524k faces and silently stops by ~397k verts/~786k faces; cutoff is on total geometry not chunk count (12 small chunks ~99k draw, 12 large ~397k do not), so splitting does not help. No per-mesh client limit below the format cap. Memory/crash never binds: no crash even at ~2.1M verts/4.2M faces in a 101 MB .3ds (contrast texture crash T3D-118). Failure is silent (whole shape vanishes, client stays up). For a server: <=~65k faces/chunk and <=a few hundred k verts/shape (~265k safe); torque/3d-mesh-size-limit-420r6-2026-11-26.md

question: What bandwidth and tick rate does a single 3D player use: outbound move/update rate and bytes per second each direction, idle vs moving?
why_it_matters: Capacity planning for a 3D server.
how_to_test: Lab 4.20r6 single client: capture the UDP+TCP streams idle and during scripted movement; measure updates/s and bytes/s each way.
status: answered (lab 4.20r6 single client, loopback pcap): ~5 packets/s and ~50-60 B/s EACH DIRECTION at steady state, a fixed low cadence movement does NOT change (the control object reports its position in every packet at a fixed ~2-3 Hz, so moving changes values not rate). 3D UDP link: client->server ~2-3 pk/s ~26-31 B/s, server->client ~1-2 pk/s ~7-13 B/s; game TCP ~2-3 pk/s ~12-18 B/s each way. Idle approximately equals moving. Only heavy traffic is a one-time few-KB scene/ghost download at join; no frame-rate-coupled stream. For a server: budget ~50-60 B/s and ~5 pk/s per 3D player each way plus a few-KB join download. torque/3d-capacity-budget-420r6-2026-11-26.md

question: Does the server trust a 3D client's self-reported control-object position — can a client teleport or send a fabricated position, and does the server accept/relay it?
why_it_matters: Anti-cheat: whether position is client-authoritative.
how_to_test: Probe 4.20r6 single client: script the control object to jump/fake a position; check what the server accepts and echoes (extends T3D-111).
status: answered (lab 4.20r6 single client): position is CLIENT-AUTHORITATIVE -- no validation. The gserver stores the control object as its updates describe it, the client reports its position in every packet, and there is no speed/delta/teleport check; a scripted teleport (impossible delta) was NOT rejected (server kept the self-reported position). No anti-cheat (extends T3D-111). For a server: do not trust a 3D client position; add server-side speed/position sanity checks -- the path accepts arbitrary teleports. torque/3d-session-lifecycle-420r6-2026-11-26.md

question: After a dropped link, does a 3D client reconnect, and does server-side 3D state (position, ghosts, control object) persist or reset on rejoin?
why_it_matters: Reconnect UX and state continuity.
how_to_test: Lab 4.20r6 single client: drop then rejoin; compare position/ghost state before and after (extends T3D-027/T3D-108).
status: answered (lab 4.20r6 single client): NO session resume. The 3D link times out after 30s of silence (TIMEOUT_MS=30000) and tears down with no reconnect/resume handshake; per-session state (control object, ghosts) is tied to the connection, so a rejoin re-enters via login+warp and rebuilds from the world (ghosts re-sent, control re-created, 3D state reset) -- the server keeps nothing session-specific across the gap. (Read from the gserver timeout/teardown + login-warp rebuild; harness runs one session/launch so a live mid-session drop+rejoin was not orchestrated.) For a server: no transport-level 3D persistence across reconnect -- do "resume where you were" at the world/script layer. torque/3d-session-lifecycle-420r6-2026-11-26.md

question: How does a 3D session reach the server through the account login and list server: the account auth, the '3 '-prefixed list entry, and the Login-server 178 warp?
why_it_matters: The real entry path a client takes into 3D.
how_to_test: Lab 4.20r6 single client: trace login via the list/Login server into a '3 ' server; record the steps (extends T3D-059).
status: answered (lab 4.20r6 single client): 3D entry = gen-5 account login -> a "3 "-prefixed 178 warp -> a dual TCP+UDP link. (1) client connects to the login server and sends the gen-5 mode-3 account login (zlib, key byte, account/password); (2) the login/list server answers with PLO_SERVERWARP (178) to a list entry whose NAME STARTS WITH "3 " (the 3D marker, e.g. "3 Lab 3D"), carrying host:port; (3) the client opens the 3D session on the listed port: a TCP login + a UDP 3D link (dual-link), and the UDP link is NOT re-authenticated (opened only for an account already logged in over TCP). For a server: authenticate on the TCP side; the UDP link rides the authenticated TCP session. torque/3d-session-lifecycle-420r6-2026-11-26.md

question: Does a 5.12-class 3D client leak memory over a sustained session (growth over tens of minutes / extrapolated to hours), or is RSS stable?
why_it_matters: Long-run stability for always-on 3D clients.
how_to_test: Lab 4.20r6 single client: hold a 3D session with periodic script activity; sample RSS over time; report slope.
status: answered (lab 4.20r6 single client): memory is STABLE, no leak. A ~15-min session with per-second script activity (overlay images/text + a positional sound call), RSS sampled every 20s (45 samples): warm-up ~122 MB -> ~138 MB by +60s, then flat in a ~0.5 MB band around ~141 MB through +900s; slope ~0 MB/min, extrapolates to holding ~141 MB indefinitely. For a server: a long-lived 3D client with ongoing script activity holds a stable ~141 MB, no per-minute leak to budget against. torque/3d-capacity-budget-420r6-2026-11-26.md

question: How does our Frankenstein 6.037 build differ from the stock 6.03r7 RETAIL client (the packed QPlay/Themida 6.0 stub), beyond the stock-6.00 comparison in T3D-122?
why_it_matters: Positions our build against what a real 6.03r7 user runs.
how_to_test: Static: compare our 6.037 build against the stock 6.03r7 retail/packed stub (skipped-v6-read) and the unpacked 6.00 engine (T3D-121/122), conceptual only.
status: answered (static, bin): comparing our Frankenstein 6.037 against what a real 6.03r7 user runs (the packed Graal 6.0.3.7.exe upload, skipped-v6-read) rather than the unpacked 6.00 engine of T3D-122. Two deltas. (1) PACKAGING/TRANSPORT (new here): the retail client is a multi-layer PACKED binary -- a self-decrypting breakpoint stub, scrambled section names, and a QPlay/CyaSSL (wolfSSL) TLS+compression export surface (SSLv3 client, RSA/ARC4/MD5/SHA, zlib; export dir named QPlay.exe while the version resource says Graal.exe); our build is a plain UNPACKED native executable with ordinary C++ symbols, no packer markers, and NO CyaSSL/QPlay secure-transport layer -- its 3D half is the plaintext proto-24 UDP+TCP dual link, so ours does not reproduce the retail secure channel. (2) 3D (same verdict as T3D-122): under the packer the retail is the Quattro 2D engine (no Torque class set, no proto-24 -- T3D-121 read the unpacked 6.03r7 directly, byte-identical to graal603.exe), while ours adds the whole proto-24 3D stack (3-server entry, dual-link handshake, login steps 2-6, GameObject/Camera ghosts, control object, sky, terrain), box-view render only. question: What is the exact byte-level framing of the proto-24 UDP 3D link — packet header, reliability/sequencing (is it TGE's NetConnection move/ack scheme?), and fragmentation?

No packet fragmentation — large payloads are chunked at the event layer (BigDataStart+Chunk, TerrainChunkEvent). Create carries the full mask, update only dirty sections, delete = kill flag with no body. Entries tracked against the packet notify (lost ones re-sent); an index is freed only after its delete is acked, then reused; own object + Camera keep their indexes across world switches. torque/3d-replica-wire-157-160-165-512-2026-11-26.md

question: What is the minimum viable replica handshake — the smallest set of packets a replica client must send to be accepted by a compatible server and appear to other real clients?
why_it_matters: Defines the interop contract: the least a replica must get right to join a real session.
how_to_test: Lab: drive a minimal scripted/synthetic client against the gserver; add packets until it links and is ghosted to a real client; record the minimal set.
status: answered (lab, ~400-line synthetic proto-24 client vs seihai-gserver main 5cd9c15, loopback, + a real 5.12 in the same world): minimum accepted handshake = gen-5 TCP login -> UDP challenge -> connect request (digest echo, proto 24/24, "Graal3D") -> first data packet with a real first-person game section -> per-packet acks carrying plain-text MissionStartPhase1Ack/Phase2Ack RemoteCommandEvents (class 5, arg type 1); server then delivers the control object; to appear to others the client emits a GameObject section-4 transform each packet and a real 5.12 ghosts it + tracks its live position (server logs 0 moves - proto-24 position rides in the game section); ghost section need not be decoded to join and is uniformly length-delimited so unknown classes skip. torque/3d-min-handshake-164-512-2026-11-26.md

question: Over the Graal file protocol, are .3ds/.dts/.png/.ttf/.wav shipped raw or wrapped (headers, compression, name-mangling) — what exactly must a replica asset loader parse off the wire?
why_it_matters: A replica loader needs the exact on-wire asset envelope, not just the base format.
how_to_test: Lab single client: capture each asset type as fetched; compare the on-wire bytes to the raw file; note any wrapper/compression/name transform (extends T3D-090).
status: answered (lab, instrumented 5.12 session): fetched .3ds/.png/.wav/.ttf are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the on-disk files once the gen5 frame is decoded. Each goes PLO_RAWDATA(length) then PLO_FILE: GInt5 modtime, length-prefixed name, file bytes, trailing newline; a large file via LARGEFILESTART+LARGEFILESIZE+N PLO_FILE pieces that concatenate exactly; .png asked/answered by bare name (no extension). The gen5 transport frame is compressed+encrypted (an 8416B body went out as 253B) but there is NO file-level wrapping, per-file compression, or name mangling beyond bare-name requests. torque/3d-replica-wire-157-160-165-512-2026-11-26.md
